request.what: Phase 1 of 2 for Bifrost, a permissionless Bitcoin-Cardano bridge, covering hardening, security audits, formal verification, ecosystem and partner readiness, and stewardship/economic foundations required for launch readiness.

claims.claim: Bifrost requests ₳12,332,031, approximately $1,973,125 at 0.16 USD/ADA including a 10% refundable contingency, for a 9-month Phase 1 delivery period.
Bifrost is designed as a permissionless Bitcoin-Cardano bridge that brings BTC onto Cardano as fBTC, a native Cardano asset usable in trading, lending, collateral, and other DeFi use cases.
By the end of Phase 1, Bifrost will be an audited bridge running on Cardano mainnet in federated and SPO-threshold custody modes under controlled access.

The proposal states Bifrost custody is distributed across 400+ Cardano SPOs weighted by delegation, requiring a cryptographic threshold of SPOs representing the majority of delegated stake to move funds.
The bridge is already live on testnet under Catalyst Fund 14, with working peg-ins and peg-outs and participating SPOs.
Catalyst Fund 14 funded Bifrost for ₳739,000 with 585 votes approved, and listed deliverables of architecture, testnet MVP, and documentation on a Dec 2025 to Aug 2026 timeline stated as on track.
Bifrost’s smart contracts, off-chain tooling, and SDK are released under Apache 2.0 for audit, forking, running, or permissionless building.
The proposer states there is no separate Bifrost token, no founder allocation, and no built-in protocol revenue claim for the founding teams.
The proposer targets 1,200 BTC TVL, about 600,000 annual transactions, and 3,000 fBTC-holding wallets by Q2 2029 as Cardano 2030 KPI contributions.
The proposer states bridge fee surplus will be returned to the Cardano Treasury in fBTC and split with SPOs after funding operations.

summary: The document requests ₳12,332,031 for Phase 1 launch-readiness work on Bifrost, a Bitcoin-Cardano bridge by FluidTokens and Lantr Engineering, with claims centered on SPO-threshold custody, Cardano-native fBTC, audits/formal verification, open-source public infrastructure, Catalyst testnet traction, and future ecosystem adoption and treasury-revenue benefits.
